findings.description: none: Package implementation centralizes shared ownership/replay semantics in docs/guides/state-artifacts.md and keeps the six workflow skills as thin repository-relative references, with no duplicated five-class inventory tables remaining in those skill sources. Task 3.2 consumed main's openspec_paths helper/guard via merge 34d8c330 without creating package-local path infrastructure, matching design D1/D4 and write_allow.

none: Spec scenarios are met: five-class inventory with required fields; eight-stage rehydration order pinned identically in the guide, design.md (via change_dir), and supervise; advisory-vs-canonical conflict and missing-state fail-loud rules present; six skills reference docs/guides/state-artifacts.md. Independently verified: 16 state-artifact tests + openspec_paths suite = 719 passed; ruff clean on the changed test; openspec validate --strict --all 90/90; install.sh --check passed; context-impact --base 4f794962 VALID/rationalized.

none: Skills use bare backticked repository-relative docs/guides/state-artifacts.md references rather than Markdown links that escape the skill directory, preserving install payload portability. Local .agents/.claude mirrors are byte-identical to the six canonical sources, and bash skills/install.sh --check passed.

none: Guide and supervise correctly separate first-run absence (valid never-started) from claimed-progress-without-canonical-artifact (fail-loud degradation), and forbid reconstructing loop-state/checkpoint truth from handoffs, learnings, phase records, or queue projections.

none: Missing/conflict paths are required to be named and reported; writer ordering persists authoritative artifacts before projections/handoffs; projection rebuild is explicitly one-way from canonical state, giving operators a recoverable interruption model without promoting derived state.

none: Documentation-only package stays within declared deny boundaries (no agent-coordinator/src, database, or apps writes in package-authored commits), introduces no authz/secret/executable attack surface, and remains rollback-safe as a pure docs/test revert. Security axis reviewed: no vulnerabilities identified.

none: Drift guards are structural string/order assertions over a small fixed file set; the focused state-artifact plus openspec_paths verification completed in about 1.57s for 719 tests, appropriate for default CI collection.

Nit: After task 3.2 normalized shared-semantics wording from "link" to "reference" (guide skill-contract line and skill reference tests), skills/supervise/SKILL.md still says "the guide linked above" even though the authority pointer is a bare backticked path, not a Markdown link.
findings.resolution: Replace "guide linked above" with "guide referenced above" (or equivalent) to match the repository-relative reference form.

findings.description: Optional: Task 2.2 requires the documentation index to reference the canonical guide, and docs/guides/documentation.md does, but skills/tests/state-artifacts/test_state_artifacts_guide.py only asserts the six skill sources. Index drift would not fail the structural suite.
findings.resolution: Add a one-line assertion that docs/guides/documentation.md contains docs/guides/state-artifacts.md or the relative state-artifacts.md link.

findings.description: FYI: Per-package context checkpoint remains degraded because checkpoint.load_package() drops the feature-level contracts block and can falsely label the approved API rationale as spurious_rationale. Base-relative validate_context_impact.py --base 4f794962 is VALID/rationalized; absence of a fresh checkpoint is not a hidden package pass. Documented in impl-findings.md as shared-infrastructure follow-up, out of package scope.
